builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Faulty Claims to Incorrect Patches: An Empirical Study of Task-Grounded Reasoning in Coding Agents
summary: This replaces task-agnostic agent-trajectory failure heuristics, such as repeated actions, with claim-level diagnosis that extracts atomic task-grounded claims from the CoT, verifies them against gathered evidence, and links defects to faulty claims through claim-corrected replay. The cost is substantial: an additional LLM extraction and evidence-gathering pass per trajectory plus manual confirmation in the study, with only 18.5% of CoT tokens being task-grounded and 191 claims per trajectory to process. It can fail as a production signal because faulty claims appear in 96.7% of resolved trajectories, so detection alone does not indicate failure and value depends on pinpointing the few causally linked claims.
rationale: The paper is diagnostic rather than a deployable inference-time method, and its evaluated pipeline relies on manual tracing plus extra LLM-agent analysis that is not yet a practical production adoption for a small team.

claims.statement: This replaces task-agnostic agent-trajectory failure heuristics, such as repeated actions, with claim-level diagnosis that extracts atomic task-grounded claims from the CoT, verifies them against gathered evidence, and links defects to faulty claims through claim-corrected replay. The cost is substantial: an additional LLM extraction and evidence-gathering pass per trajectory plus manual confirmation in the study, with only 18.5% of CoT tokens being task-grounded and 191 claims per trajectory to process. It can fail as a production signal because faulty claims appear in 96.7% of resolved trajectories, so detection alone does not indicate failure and value depends on pinpointing the few causally linked claims.
Two thirds of 188 incorrect patches trace to faulty CoT claims; correcting a linked claim fixes the defect in 89.0% of cases, and correcting all linked faulty claims resolves 11.7% of failed tasks.
